attribution.reason: Within the six sampled holding rows every tip speed (0.635-1.581 m/s) exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, while the smallest sampled position error (0.00764 m) is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest (0.05814 m) is not; the failing criterion in that window therefore includes a speed criterion that fails even where position is momentarily inside tolerance. Only six summarized rows and no paired per-row table were displayed, so this remains a bounded, testable characterization rather than a dominant-cause claim.

Recorded co-occurrence: mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s against a 0.01 s control period, with 35 deadline_misses over 35 updates, and per-update optimization_solve_s of about 15 s at several distinct updates. This documents that synchronous update computation exceeds the control period while every update is flagged as a deadline miss; synchronous wall overruns do not by themselves establish skipped simulated updates, and no causal link to the holding outcome is established here.

The selected one-step prediction batches compare a projected GVS endpoint against a full serial-backend endpoint, not full state agreement, and cover only part of the trajectory; a projected-model probe over one control step cannot explain an entire settling outcome. The observed holding speeds (0.635-1.581 m/s) are reported only as a six-row summary, with no paired per-row comparison against projections in this context.

Long optimization solve times of similar magnitude (~15.0-15.7 s) are recorded at several distinct updates (not one point), so the ~17.26 s mean update duration is not an artifact of a single anomalous update.

facts.statement: Terminal instant (single sample): terminal tip position error is 0.007642608585867386 m, which is inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance reported by the motion-view summary, and the run summary reports reach_passed = true while sampled_settling_passed = false. The identical numeric value (0.007642608585867386 m) is also the minimum error reported for the final holding window (detail.late_motion[5].error_m); cataloged late-row error samples include 0.03407510504995951 m at another row. Coverage: one terminal instant plus the six-row holding summary, not the whole trajectory.

Final holding window (t = 0.30-0.35 s; all six recorded samples, row_count = 6): tip position error spans 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m and tip speed spans 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s, against the settling limits 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s. sampled_settling_passed = false and holding_speed_passed = false. Every one of the six sampled tip speeds exceeds the 0.02 m/s speed limit, while the smallest sampled position error (0.00764 m) is inside the 0.01 m position limit and the largest (0.05814 m) exceeds it. Coverage: these six sampled rows only; not whole-trajectory ranges.

The holding-window summary reports a row count (6) and separate error and speed ranges only; no paired per-row (error, speed) table was displayed in this context, so whether sampled holding error and sampled holding speed vary together or independently across those six rows is not determinable from the selected summaries. Cataloged per-row error leaves for late rows include 0.03407510504995951 m and the 0.007642608585867386 m minimum. The sampled backend record is retained, but only the final-window rows and batched endpoint samples were displayed here.

Across the 35 recorded controller updates: mean_update_s = 17.26331904856488 s against a 0.01 s control period, deadline_misses = 35, and update_count = 35; configured max_iterations = 120. Cataloged per-update optimization_solve_s leaves are ~15 s at several distinct updates (15.002923699794337 s, 15.072048399830237 s, 15.335863699903712 s, 15.67215109989047 s, 15.079233200056478 s). Coverage: scalar run summary plus the per-update solve-time leaves present in this catalog; per-update effective_horizon and solver/optimization status values are only partly in the catalog, and the raw motion gzip cannot be read as JSON.

limitations: Coverage per area: terminal reach = single terminal instant (retained summary); sampled holding position and sampled holding speed = the six recorded rows of the 0.30-0.35 s window only; computation = run-level scalars plus the per-update solve-time/status leaves present in this catalog. Trajectory-wide statements cover only the batched prediction intervals displayed in this context (updates 0-34 in five batches).

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability is available; the prediction views return projected GVS states with bounded horizon, not full backend replay, so no dominant cause is established.
Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent), limiting per-update attribution of solve duration and plan acceptance.
The fact catalog is a compact selection of scalar leaves; per-row values not listed are not asserted, and derived counts/ranges are quoted with their stated row coverage.

Terminal-instant values are kept distinct from holding-window samples; the coincidence of the terminal error value with the minimum holding-window error (and of the terminal speed value with the minimum holding-window speed) is a numeric equality in the reported values, not evidence of a causal link.
